item.title: Ratu Peceli Rokorolovo sentenced to life imprisonment for murder of Dr Leli Darling
item.description: Lautoka High Court Judge Justice Aruna Aluthge said between 31st August and 1st September last year, Rokorolovo went to Dr Biumaitotoya’s residence in Martintar, Nadi, to collect $1,000 which had been promised to him. He said an argument followed, during which Rokorolovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife.
item.content:encoded:
Lautoka High Court Judge Justice Aruna Aluthge said between 31st August and 1st September last year, Rokorolovo went to Dr Biumaitotoya’s residence in Martintar, Nadi, to collect $1,000 which had been promised to him.

He said an argument followed, during which Rokorolovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife.

Following the attack, Rokorolovo fled the scene in Dr Biumaitotoya ’s vehicle.

He said Dr Biumaitotoya sustained multiple injuries, including three fatal chop wounds to the back of his head resulting in his death.

The court heard evidence that Rokorolovo and Dr Biumaitotoya were in a relationship which involved issues relating to financial dependence, jealousy, alcohol abuse and escalating conflict.

Justice Aluthge said evidence from family members, neighbours, police officers, medical personnel, forensic experts and witnesses relating to digital evidence and admissions made by the accused were also heard in court.

Rokorolovo raised claims of self-defence and provocation which was rejected by Justice Aluthge and found his account of self-defence implausible and unsupported by the physical evidence, and held that the force used was excessive and disproportionate.

The Court also found no credible evidence of a sudden loss of self-control sufficient to establish provocation as claimed by Rokorolovo .

Co n sidering the nature and number of the injuries inflicted, the use of a deadly weapon, and the accused’s conduct following the attack, including fleeing the scene in the deceased’s vehicle and failing to seek assistance, the Court was satisfied that Rokorolovo intended to kill Dr Biumaitotoya .

Justice Aluthge sentenced Rokorolovo today to mandatory life imprisonment, with a minimum term of 21 years to be served before a pardon may be considered.

The panelists for the public forum are Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Batiwale, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan on the theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum are Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Batiwale, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum focuses on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

item.title: 2 men charged with rape and murder of 18-year-old Lautoka woman further remanded
item.description: Tevita Tora and Laveni Vuebeti each face one count of rape and one count of murder. It is alleged that on 4th December 2025, Tora and Vuebeti raped and murdered the woman.
item.content:encoded:
Tevita Tora and Laveni Vuebeti each face one count of rape and one count of murder.

It is alleged that on 4th December 2025, Tora and Vuebeti raped and murdered the woman.

The 18-year-old was found lying motionless in a park in Lautoka.

The State has filed and served the disclosures in the case.

The two men had earlier applied for bail, however, the defence sought more time to file supplementary bail affidavit for both accused.

The matter has been adjourned to 21st September for information, plea and bail.

item.title: No one charged yet in alleged overseas employment scam involving more than 300 Fijians
item.description: Crystal Robanakadavu · 04/09/2026 Police had earlier confirmed to fijivillage News that a report has been lodged at the Namaka Police Station and an investigation is underway.
item.content:encoded:
Crystal Robanakadavu · 04/09/2026

Police had earlier confirmed to fijivillage News that a report has been lodged at the Namaka Police Station and an investigation is underway.

More than 300 people claim they paid $100 each after being promised overseas employment opportunities, with some expecting to travel to Australia.

They say over 50 people reportedly turned up at the Nadi International Airport last Saturday expecting to travel overseas but later discovered that there were no flight bookings for them.

Some of those affected had reportedly resigned from their jobs in preparation for the promised overseas employment.

The Ministry of Employment is urging those affected to lodge reports with Police and stresses that workers are not required to pay recruitment fees to participate in Government-facilitated overseas employment programmes.

item.title: Doctors urge Fijians not to wait for heart attack symptoms to worsen
item.description: Fijians are being urged not to wait until chest pain becomes unbearable before seeking medical attention, with cardiologists warning that delayed treatment can lead to more serious heart damage and complications. As Fiji observes World Heart Month under the 2026 theme, "Don't Miss a Beat", Interventional cardiologist Dr Srikar Miryala says many patients seek specialist care only after their condit
item.content:encoded:
Fijians are being urged not to wait until chest pain becomes unbearable before seeking medical attention, with cardiologists warning that delayed treatment can lead to more serious heart damage and complications.

As Fiji observes World Heart Month under the 2026 theme, "Don't Miss a Beat", Interventional cardiologist Dr Srikar Miryala says many patients seek specialist care only after their condition has significantly deteriorated or they have already suffered a heart attack.

He says recognising symptoms early and seeking immediate medical attention can improve treatment options and outcomes.

Dr Miryala says early intervention can sometimes allow patients to undergo less invasive procedures such as angioplasty or stenting.

Since March last year, he has been performing primary, or emergency, percutaneous coronary intervention procedures at PSH Hospitals.

The procedure is used to restore blood flow during a serious heart attack caused by the complete blockage of a major coronary artery, helping to minimise damage to the heart.

Dr Miryala also says substance abuse and high consumption of kava and fizzy drinks are among the other concerns contributing to heart disease in Fiji.

Award-winning cardiothoracic and vascular surgeon Dr Sanjeev Kumar Khulbey echoed the same sentiments saying that lifestyle choices are also contributing to Fijians developing heart-related conditions at younger ages.

With 30 years of experience as a cardiac specialist, Dr Khulbey says people, particularly those over 40, need to take greater responsibility for monitoring their health.

He says Fiji has access to fresh fish, fruits and vegetables, yet many people continue to rely on canned and processed foods.

According to Dr Khulbey, heart disease can be linked to lifestyle choices, existing medical conditions and genetics, although many risk factors can be reduced through healthier eating, regular exercise, avoiding tobacco and limiting alcohol consumption.

He says every household should also have a blood pressure monitor and blood sugar monitor to help people regularly keep track of their health.

Dr Khulbey is also warning people against relying on herbal medicines or homemade remedies when they are unwell, urging them to seek professional medical advice instead.
